rationale: The selected-page proposition pool reaches the full parsed-PDF best-single lexical ceiling on both grouped legacy claims and unique atoms, proving that coarse page routing already exposes the strongest available lexical evidence.

Reusing FACET_INTERLEAVED_BM25_V1 to rank propositions inside those pages regresses grouped mean F1 to 0.2607226107226107, below Wave 6 at 0.30305743036333815, and regresses unique-atom mean F1 to 0.20472730749170215, below the Wave-6 atom baseline 0.22837751648405338.
Therefore region-boundary removal/page conditioning alone is insufficient; the remaining deterministic retrieval failure is proposition-ranking/query semantics.
The result justifies research into stronger retrieval/reranking methods but does not justify a generation-model family change.

next_bounded_research: Research and predeclare a smallest-possible retrieval/reranking candidate set targeted at proposition-ranking semantics; prioritize hybrid sparse+dense/multi-vector and late-interaction methods such as BGE-M3-class retrieval and ColBERT-style scoring.
Retain current page routing and exact proposition/provenance substrate as fixed controls unless a candidate specifically demonstrates that coarse page routing is limiting.
Add semantic-support evaluation alongside the frozen lexical metric before using retrieval gains to define Wave 7.
Do not download or run external retrieval models until the candidate-selection contract is durable.
